record: P4S-VOICE-MODEL-BENCH-001 — Open-source / local STT · TTS · wake-word · VAD model benchmark PLAN + candidate matrix
mode: compile_only — benchmark DESIGN and candidate matrix ONLY; no benchmarks are run, no models are downloaded, no heavy compute is executed by this artifact

activation_gate.gate: This artifact defines the benchmark method and the candidate model matrix ONLY. Actually RUNNING the benchmark (downloading models, transcribing datasets, synthesizing audio, measuring WER/MOS/latency) is a SEPARATE, owner-called execution packet. Nothing in this artifact starts, schedules, downloads, or executes anything. Every latency / footprint / accuracy number in this artifact is flagged ESTIMATE and is a compile-time planning number, not a measurement.
activation_gate.who_gates: the owner explicitly calls the execution packet; this artifact cannot. The execution packet MUST run on an executor-role GPU node (never the orchestrator/VPS) and MUST be CPU-gated (see benchmark_method.execution_environment).

doctrine: Benchmark the local/open-source voice stack so the platform can choose STT/TTS/wake/VAD engines on measured evidence, not vendor claims. The current shipping path (umh/voice_server.py) is the BASELINE every candidate is measured against: STT = Groq whisper-large-v3-turbo (API) with faster-whisper local fallback; TTS = Kokoro on the executor GPU node (per infra/device_registry.json services.kokoro_tts:8880) with espeak fallback. Node bindings reference infra/device_registry.json ROLES (orchestrator / executor / controller), never hostnames or device-name literals. The orchestrator-role node NEVER runs a heavy model — no STT model load, no TTS model, no wake/VAD runtime beyond a network-bound API client (Node Role Discipline + CPU Gate Law).

grounding.feasibility_source: data/umh/voice/platform_voice_feasibility_matrix.json — which target can host which capability
grounding.wake_ambient_source: data/umh/voice/desktop_ambient_wake_compile.json — wake runtime candidates (openwakeword_onnx / porcupine_native) and CPU/RSS bounds
grounding.node_roles_source: infra/device_registry.json — role field decides execution host; executor nodes carry GPU + kokoro_tts service, orchestrator (VPS) is always-on coordination brain with no heavy model
grounding.governance_source: docs/VOICE_INTENT_CONTRACT.md — transcript-only transit, cloud-STT deferred to privacy review, outbound-voice governance for any voice-clone-capable TTS

node_role_discipline.law: CLAUDE.md Node Role Discipline (NON-NEGOTIABLE) + CPU Gate Law (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

orchestrator_role.allowed_voice_work: network-bound API clients ONLY (Groq STT client, a remote-TTS HTTP client). No local STT/TTS model load, no wake runtime, no VAD model that requires sustained compute. A tiny energy-threshold VAD is the only in-process voice compute permitted here.
orchestrator_role.why: the orchestrator (VPS, per registry) is the lightweight always-on coordination brain; Hostinger throttles the VPS for a week on CPU abuse (CPU Gate Law). Loading whisper/Kokoro/XTTS here is forbidden.

executor_role.allowed_voice_work: all local STT (faster-whisper / whisper.cpp / distil-whisper), all local TTS (Kokoro / Piper / XTTS), and the on-device wake runtime. Executor nodes carry the GPU and already host kokoro_tts (infra/device_registry.json services.kokoro_tts).
executor_role.why: GPU workhorse role; heavy compute belongs here

controller_role.allowed_voice_work: on-device capture + optional on-device STT/wake on the user's own device (mobile SFSpeechRecognizer / Android SpeechRecognizer, foreground wake). This is the operator's OWN hardware, not a shared UMH node, so on-device inference here does not violate UMH host discipline — but it is still governed by the feasibility matrix verdicts.
controller_role.why: controller = the operator-facing device; on-device inference runs on the operator's silicon

node_role_discipline.benchmark_host_rule: the benchmark EXECUTION packet runs on an executor-role node (GPU). It NEVER runs on the orchestrator-role node. The estimate-only matrix below annotates, per candidate, which role may host it at runtime (node_binding.runtime_host).

estimate_disclaimer: EVERY numeric value under est_latency_ms, est_footprint_mb, est_rtf, and est_accuracy in this artifact is a COMPILE-TIME ESTIMATE derived from published third-party benchmarks and model cards. NONE is a measurement taken in this environment. The execution packet replaces each estimate with a measured value on the target executor hardware. Fields carrying estimates are suffixed and every candidate carries is_estimate=true.

stt.primary_metric: WER (word error rate, lower is better)

candidates.name: groq_whisper_large_v3_turbo

est_footprint_mb.note: API client only; no model resident

candidates.quality_dimension: high accuracy, low latency, network-dependent; the CURRENT shipping default and the BASELINE all local candidates are measured against

candidates.name: faster_whisper_large_v3

est_footprint_mb.note: large-v3 ~3GB; feasible on the executor GPU (11GB VRAM class) but NOT on the VPS

governance_flags: on-device: no cloud transit; strongest privacy posture for STT

candidates.name: faster_whisper_small

node_binding.reason: small model (~500MB) still a model load; keep on executor. CPU-gated on the VPS it would burst 1-1.5 cores per umh/voice_server.py resource profile — do NOT run sustained on orchestrator.

candidates.quality_dimension: good accuracy/latency tradeoff for local fallback; the realistic local default
governance_flags: on-device

candidates.name: distil_whisper_large_v3

est_accuracy.note: distil-whisper targets ~1% WER of large-v3 while ~6x faster (published claim — VERIFY in execution packet)

candidates.name: whisper_cpp_base_en

node_binding.reason: quantized ggml base-en runs on modest CPU/Metal; may run on a controller (operator device) or executor. Sustained CPU use on orchestrator is still forbidden — do not host on VPS.

candidates.name: webgpu_whisper_transformers_js

est_footprint_mb.note: model downloaded to the browser once; runs client-side

candidates.quality_dimension: fully client-side STT — no server, no cloud, strongest privacy; constrained by browser WebGPU support (limited on mobile)
governance_flags: on-device (client browser) — audio never leaves the operator device

tts.primary_metric: MOS (mean opinion score, higher is better; subjective, measured via listening panel)

outbound_voice_governance.rule: docs/VOICE_INTENT_CONTRACT.md + outbound-voice governance: ANY TTS engine capable of ZERO/FEW-SHOT VOICE CLONING is a governance-flagged candidate. A voice-clone-capable model is NOT recommended without an explicit outbound-voice governance + licensing sign-off, because it can synthesize a target person's voice (impersonation / consent / likeness risk).
outbound_voice_governance.requirement: no clone-capable engine is RECOMMENDED by this artifact; each is listed with clone_capable=true and a governance_flag. Selecting one requires the outbound-voice governance review, NOT this benchmark.

candidates.quality_dimension: natural, fast, tiny (82M params), permissive license, no clone risk — the incumbent to beat
governance_flags: no voice-clone capability — safe under outbound-voice governance

est_accuracy.note: poor in noisy conditions; the deterministic floor

benchmark_method.principle: measure every candidate against the SAME datasets and the SAME hardware so verdicts are comparable; the current shipping engines (Groq STT, Kokoro TTS, energy VAD) are the baseline rows.

stt.primary: LibriSpeech test-clean and test-other (public, standard WER benchmark)
stt.domain: a held-out set of ~50 real UMH-style operator commands (transcript-only, synthetic/paraphrased — NEVER real recorded operator audio, per docs/VOICE_INTENT_CONTRACT.md transcript-only + no-audio-persistence policy) covering the command_router intent surface (e.g. 'approve the pending run', 'show the queue')
stt.labels: reference transcripts shipped with LibriSpeech; the domain set carries hand-written references

tts.text_set: a fixed set of ~30 sentences: short commands, long paragraphs, numbers/dates/acronyms (the hard cases for prosody)
tts.listening_panel: MOS is scored by a small human listening panel on the SAME sentences per engine; no synthetic MOS is treated as ground truth
tts.note: MOS is subjective and CANNOT be auto-measured; latency/RTF ARE measured mechanically

wake_word.positive_set: N clean + N noisy utterances of the (instance-configured) wake keyword, recorded/synthesized on-device only
wake_word.negative_set: many hours of speech + ambient audio NOT containing the keyword, to measure false-accepts per hour (public podcast/audiobook audio is an acceptable negative corpus)
wake_word.note: keyword is instance-configured at runtime, never a literal in this artifact

vad.dataset: a labelled speech/non-speech corpus (e.g. a public VAD benchmark or a segment of LibriSpeech mixed with noise at known SNRs)

execution_environment.host_selection: the execution packet resolves the target host from infra/device_registry.json by role=executor with a GPU + display; it does not hardcode a hostname
execution_environment.cpu_gate: the benchmark runner MUST call substrate.execution.cpu_gate.cpu_gate_check(caller) before each heavy model load/transcription/synthesis and MUST use gated_subprocess_run / gated_popen for any subprocess (CPU Gate Law). If the gate returns overloaded, the run PAUSES — it never saturates the host.
execution_environment.no_orchestrator_load: no STT/TTS/wake/VAD MODEL is ever loaded on the orchestrator during the benchmark; only network-bound API baselines (Groq, ElevenLabs) may be invoked from any node
execution_environment.isolation: models are downloaded and cached on the executor node's local model store (executor role = GPU workhorse per Node Role Discipline); NOTHING is downloaded or cached on the orchestrator

benchmark_method.how_to_run_cpu_gated: 1) resolve executor host from device_registry (role=executor, has GPU); 2) on the executor, for each candidate: cpu_gate_check -> load model (gated) -> run dataset -> record metric -> unload; 3) API baselines run as network clients (no model load); 4) each candidate's estimate in this matrix is REPLACED by the measured value; 5) results are written to results_location; 6) the run is idempotent and resumable so a CPU-gate pause never loses progress.

results_location.note: the EXECUTION packet writes measured results here (one JSON line per candidate per condition). This compile artifact does NOT create or write that file. Each result line carries: category, candidate, condition, metric, measured_value, host_role, measured_at, hardware_fingerprint.
results_location.created_by: execution packet only — not this artifact

forbidden_in_this_packet: running any benchmark (no transcription, no synthesis, no wake/VAD detection executed)
any heavy compute or model load on any node
any provider execution (no Groq call, no ElevenLabs call, no Kokoro synthesis) beyond referencing existing runtime logs
adding any STT/TTS/wake/VAD library to any dependency manifest
recommending a voice-clone-capable model (XTTS-v2 / ElevenLabs) without the outbound-voice governance + licensing flag
loading or hosting any heavy model on the orchestrator-role node
writing data/umh/voice/voice_model_bench_results.jsonl (that belongs to the execution packet)
any tenant or device-hostname literal as global truth — node bindings reference infra/device_registry.json roles only
